cases.content: aws_secret_access_key_hash = 2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c762e7160
cases.why: The fingerprint-of-the-secret pattern: a SHA-1 OF a credential is an artefact, not the credential. Everything a context rule reads is present — the narrow keyword, the operator, an exactly-forty body — and only the charset check refuses it: the body is one unbroken hex run, which a real base64 secret is with probability 2^-80. The mutation test pins that this case is bought by `not_pure_hex` alone (ADR 0022).

cases.content: secret_key_rotation_log: 9d5e1f4c8a7b6e5d4c3b2a1908f7e6d5c4b3a2c1 appended.
cases.why: A CI variable whose name embeds secret_key and whose value is a commit SHA. The bare secret_key keyword alternative must not turn every rotation log into a finding; the hex-run check is what keeps it silent.

cases.content: secret_id = arn:aws:secretsmanager:eu-west-1:210987654321:secret:prodDatabaseCredentialBundle/version26R7
cases.why: A Secrets Manager ARN: 'aws', 'secret:' and a slashed forty-character resource tail, all on one line — and it is the NAME of a secret, never its value. The generic keyword list fires here ('secret' + ':' + the tail), one of the measured reasons that list was refused; the shipped AWS-vocabulary keywords do not reach it (ADR 0022).

cases.content: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}
cases.why: A shell variable reference — the keyword and the operator with no value at all. The dollar and braces sit outside the body alphabet, and the inner name is twenty-one characters.

cases.content: Renseignez aws_secret_access_key = <VOTRE_CLE_SECRETE> avant le déploiement.
cases.why: A documentation placeholder in angle brackets. Nothing in it has the body's length or alphabet — which is precisely what separates a template from a leak.

cases.content: Der Token wurde widerrufen, Commit 9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2f1a0b ist deployt.
cases.why: German prose: 'Token', then a comma — which IS an operator in the vendor grammar — then a SHA two words later. The exactly-forty CONTIGUOUS body requirement keeps this silent: 'Commit ' intervenes, and the quote-run after an operator absorbs five characters at most. The refused proximity variant (any secret keyword within forty characters of a forty-char body) fires on it (ADR 0022).

cases.content: Le secret a été déplacé ; voir le commit 0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f001122334.
cases.why: French prose with 'secret' twenty characters before a commit SHA and no assignment anywhere. The refused proximity variant fires on it; the assignment grammar has no operator to find — the semicolon is not in the vendor's operator set, a boundary this corpus now records (ADR 0022).
